claim: The default launch flow uses the bundled MACE-MPA-0 model when NGC_API_KEY is set.
premises: The default launch flow uses the bundled MACE-MPA-0 model.
The bundled MACE model is auto-downloaded with an NGC API key.
For the default setup, follow the Quickstart Guide.

claim: MACE models are restricted to periodic systems and require pbc: true.
premises: MACE models are for periodic systems only (pbc: true).
The default MACE-MPA-0 model is bundled and auto-downloaded when NGC_API_KEY is set.
To use a different MACE model, download it and mount the model file or directory into the container.

claim: AIMNet2 models must be downloaded or trained externally and mounted into the container for use.
premises: AIMNet2 models are not bundled with the container.
Download or train a model and mount the model file.
For trained models, a selection of checkpoints are available for download from AIMNetCentral.

claim: TensorNet models require downloading the full model directory, not just the .pt file, and must be mounted into the container.
premises: TensorNet models are not bundled; download the model and mount it.
TensorNet models are available on matgl.
The easiest way to download a particular model directory (the entire directory, not just the .pt checkpoint file, is necessary) is to use the provided curl and tar command.

claim: Launching the container with a custom model requires setting ALCHEMI_MODEL_PATH, NIM_DISABLE_MODEL_DOWNLOAD, and ALCHEMI_NIM_MODEL_TYPE environment variables.
premises: To use a custom model, download it and mount the model file or directory into the container.
Launching the container with MACE requires setting ALCHEMI_MODEL_PATH, NGC_API_KEY, NIM_DISABLE_MODEL_DOWNLOAD, and ALCHEMI_NIM_MODEL_TYPE.
Similar environment variable patterns are used for AIMNet2 and TensorNet launches.

claim: Release 2.1.0 introduces support for the Evo 2 7B 1M model variant as a faster and more resource-efficient alternative to the 40B 1M model.
premises: This release introduces support for the Evo 2 7B 1M model variant, providing a faster and more resource-efficient option while maintaining strong accuracy for most use cases.
The 40B 1M model remains available as the default for maximum accuracy.
Added support for the Evo 2 7B 1M model variant, selectable via the NIM_VARIANT=7b environment variable.

claim: Release 2.0.0 introduced support for custom and fine-tuned checkpoints and migrated to the NVIDIA BioNeMo Framework, resulting in up to 30% faster inference workflows.
premises: This major release introduces support for loading custom and fine-tuned checkpoints, enabling users to leverage their own model weights or community-provided variants.
The internal implementation of NIM has migrated to the NVIDIA BioNeMo Framework, providing unified training and inference code bases and standardized checkpoint formats.
Thanks to the migration to the BioNeMo Framework, new Evo 2 NIM release delivers up to 30% faster inference workflows compared to the 1.x series.

claim: Release 1.0.2 improved stability in multi-GPU environments and compatibility with new NIM versions by resolving FP8 extra states issues and updating dependencies.
premises: Resolved an issue related to FP8 extra states when running on specific combinations of GPU interconnects and CPUs. The fix ensures correct handling of FP8 extra states, with additional checks to verify correct functionality.
Updated nimlib and related dependencies to improve compatibility with the latest NIM releases.

claim: Release 1.0.1 added automatic uppercase conversion of input prompts and enhanced health endpoint reporting for non-recoverable errors.
premises: The input prompt is now automatically converted to uppercase internally, helping to prevent the common mistake of supplying lowercase DNA sequences to the model.

For non-recoverable errors, such as unrecoverable memory ECC errors, the health endpoint will now reflect the error status. This allows cloud infrastructure to redeploy the instance to healthy hardware.

claim: Release 1.0.0 was the first release of Evo 2 NIM, featuring a 40 billion parameter model trained on 11 trillion DNA nucleotides with a context length of up to 1 million DNA nucleotides.
premises: This is the first release of Evo 2 NIM. Evo 2 is a biological foundation model that is able to integrate information over long genomic sequences, while retaining sensitivity to single-nucleotide changes.
This release features 40 billion parameters model trained on 11 trillion DNA nucleotides with context-length of up to 1 million DNA nucleotides.

claim: The Evo 2 NIM requires GPUs with FP8 support, such as NVIDIA H100 or H200, and recommends using the benchmarking suite to validate deployment.
premises: Ensure you use this model with GPUs that have FP8 support, such as NVIDIA H100, NVIDIA H200, or newer. For more information, see Prerequisites and Support Matrix for Evo2 NIM.
Ensure you always use the benchmarking suite so that the deployed model works as expected.

claim: To launch a Cosmos WFM NIM container, users must generate an NGC API key, export it as an environment variable, authenticate with NGC, and run a docker command with specific parameters including GPU access, cache mounting, and port forwarding.
premises: An NGC API key is required to access NGC resources and must be generated with at least NGC Catalog selected.
The NGC_API_KEY environment variable must be exported and passed to the docker run command for authentication.
The docker run command includes flags such as --runtime=nvidia, --gpus all, -e NGC_API_KEY, -v for cache mounting, and -p 8000:8000 for port forwarding.

claim: The NIM container serves an inference API endpoint on port 8000, and successful startup is indicated by specific log messages showing served endpoints including /v1/infer (POST), which can be validated via health checks and used to generate videos from text, image, or video inputs.
premises: Successful startup is indicated by log messages listing served endpoints: 0.0.0.0:8000/v1/health/live, /v1/health/ready, /v1/metrics, /v1/license, /v1/metadata, /v1/manifest, and /v1/infer (POST).
The /v1/health/live and /v1/health/ready endpoints return HTTP 200 when the server is live and ready, respectively.

Inference requests are made via POST to http://0.0.0.0:8000/v1/infer with JSON payloads containing prompt, and optionally image, video, seed, or other parameters, returning a base64-encoded video that must be decoded and saved.

claim: Specific docker run parameters are required for different Cosmos WFM NIM models, including increased shared memory and file descriptor limits for the cosmos-transfer2.5-2b model, and cache directory permissions may need adjustment to avoid download errors.
premises: The --shm-size=16GB flag is used for cosmos-predict1-7b-text2world and cosmos-predict1-7b-video2world, while cosmos-transfer2.5-2b requires --shm-size=32GB and --ulimit nofile=65536:65536 due to higher resource demands.
The -v "$LOCAL_NIM_CACHE:/opt/nim/.cache" flag mounts a local cache directory to enable model reuse across runs.
The -u $(id -u) flag ensures the container runs as the host user to prevent permission mismatches when writing to the local cache directory.

claim: Users can list available NIM containers via the NGC CLI using a specific command that outputs model metadata in CSV format, which is used to identify the correct Repository and Latest_Tag values for launching a desired NIM.
premises: The command `ngcregistryimagelist --format_type csv 'nvcr.io/nim/nvidia/cosmos**'` lists available NIMs in CSV format.
The output includes columns: Name, Repository, LatestTag, ImageSize, UpdatedDate, Permission, SignedTag?, AccessType, AssociatedProducts.
The Repository and LatestTag fields from this output are used to construct the IMG_NAME in the docker run command.

claim: NIM fails to start when the license terms on NGC are not accepted before pulling the container image and model assets.
premises: Some NIM models require that you accept the license terms on NGC before you can pull the container image and model assets.
If you attempt to start a NIM, in some cases it fails to start when you run the docker run command.

claim: The NIM for Object Detection documentation provides structured guidance for users to get started, deploy, configure, and manage the system.
premises: The documentation includes sections titled 'Get Started', 'Deploy on Kubernetes', and 'Configure'.
It contains a 'User Guide' with subsections on Observability, Optimization, Performance, Security, and Troubleshoot.
It includes a 'Reference' section with API Reference, Environment Variables, and Helm Chart Parameters.
